quote_source.name: Stock Analysis historical regular-session closes; issuer releases and SEC filings for fundamentals
quote_source.note: October 26, 2026 regular-session unadjusted closes in USD, verified from historical rows; October 27 intraday and premarket prices are deliberately excluded. Research incorporates news available October 27, including the October 26 financing announcement. No fills are inferred.

market_emotion.basis: SOXX rebounded 2.85% on October 26 after a 6.79% October 22 decline. Lam fell 11.76% after earnings and Credo fell 10.70% then 9.51% on October 22-23. A rebound does not establish a durable base. Supplier residual-value support adds financing exposure.
market_emotion.interpretation: Uncalibrated qualitative risk heat; not a second stock score, sentiment survey or probability.

strict_scoring.score_formula: forward fundamental surprise + narrative and expectation shift + supply-chain moat and diffusion + valuation and reaction gap + financial quality and positioning risk + evidence integrity
strict_scoring.interpretation: The score is an ordinal research rank, not a calibrated probability, target return, or backtested alpha estimate.
hard_gates: Current attributable earnings release and filing review
No unresolved accounting or liquidity red flag
Price and valuation considered relative to expectations
A score of at least 82 is necessary but execution also requires the stated condition
No automatic market order; the eligible list can be empty when price or evidence gates fail

position_sizing_overlay.rule: Use the conviction rank only for selection. Size is reduced independently for volatility, portfolio correlation, crowding, customer concentration, liquidity, and earnings risk.
position_sizing_overlay.initial_size: No more than about one-quarter of intended exposure for current staged buys, and only when each stated price condition is met.
position_sizing_overlay.exit_rule: Review or exit when the guidance, demand, margin, cash-flow, customer, or supply-chain thesis breaks; do not rely on price stops alone.

MU.reason: Memory remains the strongest verified profit-growth case in this sample. FY26 Q4 GAAP profit was $37.701B; the September 3 year-end 10-K reports $74.33 diluted annual EPS. At $903.70 the annual earnings multiple is 12.2x, but peak pricing and margins can reverse. Score unchanged.

ASML.reason: October 14 Q3 results and the 2027-2028 supply shortfall support scarce lithography capacity. The lower USD close improves the valuation factor by one point; it does not make a mixed EUR/USD P/E valid. Export controls and customer capex concentration remain risks.

NVDA.reason: The latest 10-Q supports strong compute and networking demand, while the lower reference price adds one valuation point. Investment gains, purchase commitments, model-customer funding and improving custom-ASIC software remain deductions.

LRCX.reason: New October 21 results and October 22 10-Q verify $8.219B revenue, $2.753B GAAP profit and strong cash generation. Deposition and etch benefit from DRAM and 3D complexity. The earnings sell-off creates a research opportunity, but supply constraints, China exposure and cyclical capex block an unconditional buy.

AVGO.reason: Q3 AI growth and cash flow remain strong. October 26's $63B Anthropic SPV transaction adds residual-value support equal to its first-lien financing portion. That amount and detailed loss mechanics are not disclosed in the short release. Quality/risk falls six points; do not book the financing as incremental revenue or assume the entire $63B is Broadcom debt.

CRDO.reason: The lower price adds two valuation points, but four end customers remain 84% of revenue and Q1 stock compensation was $87.979M versus $90.231M operating cash flow. New ALC and memory-connectivity products require paid deployments and yield proof, not just demonstrations.

MRVL.reason: October 6's management FY28 revenue outlook improves visibility but is not reported earnings. One valuation point is added after the pullback; customer-program concentration and conditional warrant dilution still block a buy.

KLAC.reason: Process-control demand is attractive, but the October 28 after-close earnings event is pending. Do not infer tomorrow's results from Lam's quarter or mix split-adjusted prices with pre-split EPS.

FORM.reason: The lower price improves valuation by two points, offset by one event-risk point before the October 28 report. Q2 profit growth is strong but the ten-year 10x earnings hurdle remains demanding.

PDFS.reason: Yield analytics has strategic relevance, but a small profit base, sequential platform weakness, acquisition integration and dilution limit conviction. A lower share price alone is insufficient.

strict_scoring.evidence_limitations: No point-in-time consensus database or validated backtest is available. Forward surprise is a qualitative assessment of guidance and earnings trajectory, not a measured consensus beat. Weights are unchanged; repeated coverage of one transaction is not independent evidence.

rankings.actionable_status: No unconditional buy. Prior MU, ASML and NVDA stabilization gates remain unmet at the October 26 close. Lam's new post-earnings gate is also pending. Live October 27 conditions must be rechecked.
rankings.positioning: Research priority: MU and ASML, then NVDA and LRCX. Use no more than one-quarter of intended exposure only after conditions are met. Do not lower technical gates merely because prices fell. No closing reference is a limit order or fill.

capital_flow.name: Broadcom / Anthropic SPV
capital_flow.signal: SPV buys XPU/networking and leases to Anthropic, with deliveries expected from 2027. Broadcom provides residual-value support equal to first-lien portion; tranche amount and loss mechanics not quantified in the short release. Not recognized revenue, not automatically all Broadcom debt, and not additional hyperscaler capex.

supply_chain_view.framework: Funded demand -> qualified tools and cleanrooms -> logic and memory -> packaging/test -> networked, powered racks -> useful tokens and customer cash flow
supply_chain_view.forecast_horizon: October 2026 to October 2028; analyst assessment, not a certainty
next_two_year_bottlenecks: Deposition/etch components and cleanroom availability: Lam's October call says both constrain 2027 output; demand visibility is not the same as shippable capacity
Lithography output: ASML says planned 2027 and 2028 supply will not fully meet customer demand
HBM4 qualification, DRAM process yield and multi-tier inference memory capacity
Advanced packaging, substrates and known-good-die / optical-engine testing
1.6T links, 224G signaling, lasers, fiber assembly, link telemetry and network reliability
Grid connections, transformers, 800VDC conversion, liquid-cooling qualification and powered sites
Project financing and customer cash generation: equipment demand does not guarantee funded deployment
supply_chain_view.trend: 2027-2028 likely favors qualified manufacturing capacity and memory/network attach, but constrained supply does not ensure permanent scarcity rents. Inference expands DRAM, LPDDR and NAND cache tiers; custom ASIC software improves competition with GPUs. Panel packaging and hybrid bonding are opportunities subject to yield, qualification and cost. Supplier-backed finance moves residual-value and customer-credit risk back up the chain.
